snapshot.text: Vietnam is moving towards universal health care through social health insurance, which covered about 93.4% of people in 2024. Out-of-pocket spending is still high. Politburo Resolution 72 (September 2025) is driving a shift from treatment to prevention.

priorities.title: Universal health insurance by 2030
priorities.text: A May 2026 action plan expands insurance benefits to more preventive services and check-ups. It targets over 95% coverage in 2026 and universal coverage by 2030, with basic hospital fees exempted under a roadmap.

priorities.title: Free annual health checks (Resolution 72)
priorities.text: The Health Minister presented a draft National Assembly resolution giving each resident one free check or screening a year, prioritised by group and funding. It was due to take effect on 1 January 2026. I could not confirm its adoption.

priorities.title: Grassroots workforce and digital health records
priorities.text: The Ministry of Health is prioritising training of health workers at grassroots and preventive levels. It is also promoting electronic medical records, digital health records and sector-wide databases.

netherlands.text: The Dutch NGO Medical Committee Netherlands-Vietnam (MCNV) has worked in Vietnam since 1968. Its current work includes rehabilitation workforce training. I found no current government-to-government health programme.
